bib.title: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis" (DreamGym), Zhaorun Chen, Zhuokai Zhao, Kai Zhang, Bo Liu, ... Jason Weston, Dat Huynh (Meta Superintelligence Labs, FAIR, UChicago, UNC, UC Berkeley). arXiv:2511.03773v2, Nov 2025. Preprint.

COVERAGE: All 27 pages read; 89,856 of 89,856 chars. Extraction was clean text. Reference list skimmed. The tail of the judge prompt (last few lines of C.4) was cut off in the extraction and is not needed. Figure 3 (curves/bars) has no extractable numbers; I did not render images.

CLAIMS
1. DreamGym trains agents with RL entirely on synthetic experience from an LLM "reasoning experience model", with zero real interactions.
 number: 0 real transitions
 setup: Table 1; WebShop, ALFWorld, WebArena-Lite; Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B; GRPO and PPO; experience model is Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, SFT'd.
 quote: "DreamGym 0 59.3 63.9 68.3 62.1 66.3 71.0 13.3 9.1 12.7"
 where: p7, Table 1

2. In RL-ready environments, synthetic-only training roughly matches RL on 80K real transitions. It is not uniformly better.
 number: WebShop GRPO, 80K real: 62.1/65.0/66.1 vs DreamGym 59.3/63.9/68.3 (L3.2-3B/L3.1-8B/Q2.5-7B). ALFWorld GRPO: 65.3/70.9/79.8 vs 62.1/66.3/71.0. ALFWorld PPO, Q2.5-7B: 81.1 real vs 72.7 DreamGym. ALFWorld PPO, L3.2-3B: 47.0 vs 40.5.
 setup: as claim 1.
 quote: "DreamGym-trained agents perform on par with GRPO and PPO agents trained on 80K real interactions, despite using only synthetic rollouts."
 where: p8, section 5.2 and Table 1

3. On WebArena, which is not RL-ready, DreamGym beats the real-env RL baselines.
 number: WebArena GRPO real 7.3/6.1/6.1 vs DreamGym 13.3/9.1/12.7. PPO real 6.7/4.8/7.3 vs DreamGym 14.5/10.9/10.0.
 setup: WebArena-Lite, 165 eval tasks, 647 training tasks. The real baseline was limited to four AWS servers (four parallel sessions), run on a "vanilla RL pipeline" the authors built.
 quote: "agents trained purely in DreamGym achieve success rates exceeding 30% across all backbones (Table 1)"
 where: p8. CAUTION: this text conflicts with Table 1, where the DreamGym WebArena values are 9.1-14.5. The abstract's "over 30%" is probably a relative improvement. Do not cite "30% success rate". The abstract says: "On non-RL-ready tasks like WebArena, DreamGym outperforms all baselines by over 30%." Treat that as an unclear relative gain.
 where: p1 and p8

4. Sim-to-real (DreamGym-S2R): train synthetically, then run a small real RL phase. This beats from-scratch RL on mostly all cells, using about 6% of the real data.
 number: 5K real transitions vs 80K. WebShop GRPO 70.5/75.0/72.1 vs real 62.1/65.0/66.1. ALFWorld GRPO Q2.5-7B 82.4 vs 79.8. ALFWorld PPO L3.2-3B 49.1 vs 47.0.
 setup: Table 1. Exceptions: ALFWorld GRPO L3.2-3B 65.0 vs 65.3, and WebShop PPO L3.1-8B 63.9 vs 64.2.
 quote: "This approach yields over 40% performance improvement compared to training from scratch in real-world environments while using less than 10% of the external data"
 where: p2 (intro) and p8
 note: "Over 40%" is likely a relative gain and is not defined precisely in the text.

5. Efficiency: training effort (rollout time plus GPU hours) is about a third to a fifth of real-environment RL.
 number: "one-third or even one-fifth"
 setup: WebArena, Fig. 3 left. Exact hours are not given in the text.
 quote: "reducing training effort (including both rollouts sampling time and GPU hours) to roughly one-third or even one-fifth of RL baselines in the real environment"
 where: p8

6. Ablations: every component helps (success %).
 number: Full 63.9 WebShop / 13.3 WebArena. w/o Exp. Replay 59.2 / 9.7. w/o Exp. Reasoning 55.8 / 7.3. w/o Task Generation 57.3 / 7.3.
 setup: Table 2. Backbone and RL algorithm are not stated in the caption. The 63.9 / 13.3 values match Llama-3.1-8B GRPO.
 quote: "removing the task generator leads to a 6.6% and 6.0% drop in success rate compared with the full DreamGym configuration"
 where: p9
 note: The two drops are absolute points (63.9-57.3 and 13.3-7.3), despite the "%".

7. The experience model is data-efficient: small offline sets and small backbones work.
 number: >50% WebShop with 10K offline samples (Llama-3.1-8B). About 55% with 20K samples (Llama-3.2-3B). WebDreamer about 13% on WebArena.
 setup: Fig. 5. Offline SFT data are 2K-40K transition steps. Appendix: WebShop has 1,600 human plus 2,000 oracle/random trajectories; ALFWorld 3,200 expert plus 2,000; WebArena 4,800 trajectories from leaderboard agents plus random policy.
 quote: "the Llama-3.1-8B exceeds 50% success rate with only 10k samples"
 where: p10

8. Cross-domain transfer works between web domains but fails to ALFWorld.
 number: none
 setup: Fig. 3 middle. Policy trained in DreamGym with seed tasks from WebShop transfers to WebArena and beats SFT there, and the reverse also holds. Web to ALFWorld drops "significantly".
 quote: "when the domain gap becomes too large, such as transferring from web-based environments (WebShop/WebArena) to ALFWorld (Shridhar et al.), the performance drops significantly"
 where: p8

9. Curriculum rule: select tasks by group reward variance. This is the "reward entropy" heuristic; it is variance of the outcome reward, not entropy. Sample a bounded fraction λ of synthetic tasks.
 number: formula V_τ = (1/n) Σ (r_i - r̄)^2; max when successes and failures are balanced. Outcome reward is 1 at the final step on success, else 0.
 setup: Eq. 7; for GRPO, the group G is the training group; for PPO, tasks are clustered by embedding.
 quote: "A task reaches maximum entropy when successes and failures are evenly balanced in G, providing the greatest information gain for credit assignment."
 where: p6

10. Experience model design: (s_{t+1}, r_{t+1}) is predicted by chain-of-thought, conditioned on interaction history, the task, and top-k similar transitions from a replay buffer. State space is abstract text (for example, refined AX-tree element lists, not raw HTML). The SFT loss covers the reasoning trace plus next state.
 number: none
 setup: Eqs. 4-5; reasoning traces R* are annotated by a teacher LLM.
 quote: "agent training does not require perfectly realistic environments, but rather interaction data that is sufficiently diverse, informative, and causally grounded to acquire knowledge for the target task"
 where: p2
 Judge check (GPT-4o, 100 trajectories, scores 0-2, Fig. 4): removing history hurts consistency; removing reasoning hurts informativeness and raises hallucination. Bar values are not in the text.

11. Theory: a lower bound on real-environment improvement from synthetic training.
 number: gap Δ_model = ε_R/(1-γ) + 2γR_max ε_P/(1-γ)^2. Trust-region penalty 4γ(1-γ)^-2 V_max δ.
 setup: Theorem 1 and Lemma 1, Appendix B. Assumes bounded reward error ε_R, sup-TV transition error ε_P, and a KL trust region (as in PPO/GRPO).
 quote: "the gap of agent performance between real and synthetic environments depends only on reward accuracy and domain consistency errors, rather than on strict fidelity metrics such as state reconstruction error"
 where: p18
 Caveat: the bound is vacuous unless the sup-errors are small. The text only asserts that "both εR and εP can be made very small"; no measurement is reported.

12. Training curves: on WebShop the success rate rises faster in the first 40 steps and variance is smaller than for real-environment baselines.
 number: 40 steps
 setup: Fig. 3 right.
 quote: "the success rate improves much more rapidly within the first 40 steps"
 where: p9

LIMITS
- The authors concede only one limit: single-environment setups; a universal multi-environment world model is future work (p11).
- The authors say transfer to ALFWorld fails when the domain gap is large.
- The WebArena real-RL baseline is weak by construction. It runs on four AWS servers, keeps flawed trajectories and evaluator errors "as-is", and uses a self-built pipeline. The headline gain over it is therefore partly an infrastructure artifact.
- The text and Table 1 disagree on WebArena ("exceeding 30%" success vs 9-15% in the table). The "over 30%" and "over 40%" claims are undefined relative gains.
- No seeds, error bars or significance tests appear in the text.
- The experience model is Llama-3.1-8B only; the judge is a single GPT-4o prompt on WebShop, 100 trajectories.
- The reward is outcome-only, binary, and produced by the learned model. Reward accuracy (ε_R) is never measured against the real environment.
- Data comes from leaderboard agents, which could leak distribution information. Test tasks were held out.
- Compute: 8 A100 nodes plus 4 H100 nodes. Synthetic-model serving cost is not reported separately.
- ALFWorld is run in its TextWorld text setup.

BUILDS ON
- PPO (Schulman et al., 2017) and GRPO (Shao et al., 2024), used as the RL algorithms.
- Trust-region bound (Schulman et al., 2015), for Theorem 1.
- verl-agent / GiGPO (Feng et al., 2025), for the outcome reward and baselines.
- World models: Ha and Schmidhuber 2018; Dreamer (Hafner et al., 2020).
- LLM-as-simulator: WebDreamer (Gu et al., 2024); WebEvolver (Fang et al., 2025); UI-Simulator (Wang et al., 2025b), which the authors call the closest work.
- Task synthesis: Self-Challenging agents (Zhou et al., 2025); AgentSynth (Xie et al., 2025); Synatra (Ou et al., 2024); AgentTrek (Xu et al.).
- Curriculum: WebRL (Qi et al., 2024); Prompt Curriculum Learning (Gao et al., 2025), which supports the finding that LLMs learn best from intermediate difficulty.
- "Era of experience" (Silver and Sutton, 2025); Agent Learning via Early Experience (Zhang et al., 2025).
- Benchmarks: WebShop (Yao et al., 2022), ALFWorld (Shridhar et al.), WebArena (Zhou et al.), WebArena-Lite (Liu et al., 2024).

CODE: none (prompt templates only, pp19-26). Useful template: the WebShop reasoning-annotation prompt (p19) asks for a task_tutorial with Overall Plan, Success Mode and Failure Mode, plus per-step "transition_plan" entries. The task-variation selection prompt (pp20-23) asks for "the most challenging yet feasible variation" in the format "SELECTION: [number] REASONING: [explanation]".

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p1): contrasts the traditional agent-environment loop with the experience-model loop. Good for orientation.
- Fig. 2 (p4): the architecture. Agent, reasoning experience model, replay buffer (top-k retrieve and update), curriculum task generator (reward-entropy task value), CoT reasoning. This is the best single explainer.
- Fig. 3 (p8): left, WebArena success vs wall-clock/GPU time; middle, cross-domain transfer; right, WebShop success vs training steps for Traditional, DreamGym w/o Task, DreamGym, S2R.
- Fig. 4 (p9): GPT-4o judge scores on consistency, diversity, informativeness and hallucination, comparing Traditional, DreamGym, w/o History and w/o Reasoning.
- Fig. 5 (p10): experience-model success vs offline sample size and backbone.
- Fig. 6 (p10): a WebArena case study with synthetic state generation and <think> reasoning.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table 1 and Table 2 text extractions are readable, but column grouping relied on the caption order (L3.2-3B, L3.1-8B, Q2.5-7B per environment). The 30%/40% statements are inconsistent with the table values (see claim 3). Fig. 3-5 values are not extractable from text.
